# libtmux for Raku [![CI](https://github.com/libtmux/libtmux-raku/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/libtmux/libtmux-raku/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![LibTmux](https://raku.land/zef:libtmux/LibTmux/badges/version)](https://raku.land/zef:libtmux/LibTmux) [![license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue)](https://github.com/libtmux/libtmux-raku/blob/master/LICENSE)
Start a private tmux server, split panes, send input, find panes with plain Raku predicates, and react to terminal output as it arrives. ## Install Needs Raku 6.d or newer, tmux 3.3a or newer and Linux. Install from [Raku Land][raku-land] with its Fez authority: ```console $ zef install 'LibTmux:auth' ``` To install a checkout instead: ```console $ zef install . ``` The [toolchain guide][repo-github-contributing-md-toolchain] covers Raku and zef setup. The [changelog][repo-changelog-md] lists each release. ## Create sessions and panes ### [`Server.start`][api-server-start] and [`PaneRef.split`][api-pane-split]: create and arrange panes Start a private server, split its first pane and title both panes. Each runs `cat`, and `LEAVE` closes the server on any exit. [`Server.new-session`][api-server-new-session] and [`SessionRef.new-window`][api-session-new-window] add sessions and windows. ```raku use LibTmux; my $server = Server.start(:name, :shell-command('exec cat')); LEAVE $server.close if $server.defined; my $before = $server.snapshot; my $left = $before.panes.single.ref; my $right = $left.split(:horizontal, :shell-command('exec cat')); $left.set-title('editor'); $right.set-title('logs'); my $after = $server.snapshot; my $editor = $after.panes.filter(*.title eq 'editor').single; say "{$editor.title}: {$after.panes.elems} panes"; ``` It prints `editor: 2 panes`. The earlier snapshot still has one pane: `.ref` commands change tmux, while a snapshot keeps what it captured. Save it as `quickstart.raku` and run it: ```console $ raku quickstart.raku ``` From a checkout: ```console $ raku -I. examples/quickstart.raku ``` More: the [native API guide][repo-lib-libtmux-rakumod]. ## Resize and remove panes ### [`PaneRef.resize`][api-pane-resize] and [`PaneRef.kill`][api-pane-kill]: size and remove panes Split a pane, size the window and the first pane, then kill the second pane. [`WindowRef.resize`][api-window-resize] sizes a window. A window, a session and the daemon go with [`WindowRef.kill`][api-window-kill], [`SessionRef.kill`][api-session-kill] and [`Server.kill-server`][api-server-kill-server]. ```raku use v6.d; use LibTmux; sub MAIN(Str:D :$tmux = 'tmux') { my $server = Server.start(:binary($tmux), :name, :width(120), :height(30), :shell-command('exec cat')); LEAVE $server.close if $server.defined; my $before = $server.snapshot; my $window = $before.windows.single.ref; my $editor = $before.panes.single.ref; my $logs = $editor.split(:horizontal, :shell-command('exec cat')); $window.resize(:width(100), :height(20)); $editor.resize(:width(30)); my $sized = $server.snapshot; say "window: {$sized.windows.single.width}x{$sized.windows.single.height}"; say "editor: {$sized.panes.where(%(id => $editor.id)).single.width} columns"; $logs.kill; say "panes: {$server.snapshot.panes.elems}"; } ``` It prints `window: 100x20`, `editor: 30 columns` and `panes: 1`. - `resize` takes `:width` and `:height`, or `:direction` with `:amount`. It refuses a mix of the two. More: the [native API guide][repo-lib-libtmux-rakumod]. ## Query captured panes ### [`PaneSelection.where`][api-pane-selection-where]: select panes from a snapshot Select wide panes with query data, then find `editor` with a Raku predicate through [`filter`][api-pane-selection-filter]. Native `.grep`, `.map` and `.sort` list the rest. [`Server.query-panes`][api-server-query-panes] asks tmux for a fresh selection instead of reading a snapshot. ```raku use v6.d; use LibTmux; sub MAIN(Str:D :$tmux = 'tmux') { my $server = Server.start(:binary($tmux), :name, :width(160), :height(40), :shell-command('exec cat')); LEAVE $server.close if $server.defined; my $editor = $server.snapshot.panes.single.ref; my $tests = $editor.split(:horizontal, :shell-command('exec cat')); my $logs = $tests.split(:shell-command('exec cat')); $editor.set-title('editor'); $tests.set-title('tests'); $logs.set-title('logs'); my $snapshot = $server.snapshot; my @wide := $snapshot.panes.where(%(width => %(gte => 60))); my $selected = @wide.filter(*.title eq 'editor').single; say "Wide pane: {$selected.title}"; my @others = $snapshot.panes.grep(*.id ne $selected.id).map(*.title).sort; say 'Other panes: ' ~ @others.join(', '); } ``` It prints `Wide pane: editor` and `Other panes: logs, tests`. - Bind with `:=` to keep a typed selection; `=` makes a plain array. - `where` checks fields and operators; `filter` returns the same selection type. - `.single` wants exactly one match, `.single-or-nil` allows none. `.one` stays Raku's junction. More: the [native API guide][repo-lib-libtmux-rakumod] covers relations and portable filters. ## Choose where a query runs ### [`Server.explain-panes`][api-server-explain-panes]: what tmux filters and what Raku filters [`Server.query-panes`][api-server-query-panes] takes `:pushdown`: - `auto` (the default) has tmux apply the restrictions it can match exactly, then rechecks every result in Raku. - `never` lists first and filters in Raku. - `require` throws when any part would stay local. ```raku use v6.d; use LibTmux; sub MAIN(Str:D :$tmux = 'tmux') { my $server = Server.start(:binary($tmux), :name, :shell-command('exec cat')); LEAVE $server.close if $server.defined; $server.snapshot.panes.single.ref.set-title('editor'); my %wide = width => %(gte => 60); my %titled = AND => [%wide, %(title => %(contains => 'edit'))]; say 'width: fully pushed = ' ~ $server.explain-panes(:where(%wide)).fully-pushed; my $plan = $server.explain-panes(:where(%titled)); say 'width and title: fully pushed = ' ~ $plan.fully-pushed; say 'tmux filter: ' ~ $plan.source-filter; say 'Matches: ' ~ $server.query-panes(:where(%titled)).map(*.title).join(', '); try { $server.query-panes(:where(%titled), :pushdown); CATCH { when X::LibTmux::Unsupported { say 'require: refused, title stays local' } } } } ``` It prints: ```text width: fully pushed = True width and title: fully pushed = False tmux filter: #{e|>=:#{pane_width},60} Matches: editor require: refused, title stays local ``` More: the [native API guide][repo-lib-libtmux-rakumod]. ## Adapt to the running daemon ### [`Capabilities.supports`][api-capabilities-supports]: choose a supported operation Create an empty `status` pane: floating when the daemon supports it, tiled otherwise. [`Snapshot.capabilities`][api-snapshot-capabilities] holds what the daemon, not the client binary, can do. [`Options.describe`][api-options-describe] gives an option's type, scopes and first release; [`Server.options`][api-server-options] and [`Server.hooks`][api-server-hooks] read and set options and hooks. ```raku use v6.d; use LibTmux; sub MAIN(Str:D :$tmux = 'tmux') { my $server = Server.start(:binary($tmux), :name, :width(120), :height(36), :shell-command('exec cat')); LEAVE $server.close if $server.defined; my $snapshot = $server.snapshot; my $main = $snapshot.panes.single.ref; my $floating = $snapshot.capabilities.supports('pane-floating'); my $auxiliary = $floating ?? $main.new-floating(:width(40), :height(12), :x(2), :y(2), :empty) !! $main.split(:horizontal, :empty); $auxiliary.set-title('status'); my $after = $server.snapshot; die 'The auxiliary pane was not captured' unless $after.panes.elems == 2; say 'Status pane: ' ~ ($floating ?? 'floating' !! 'tiled'); say $after.panes.where(%(id => $auxiliary.id)).single.title; } ``` It prints `Status pane: floating` or `Status pane: tiled`, then `status`. More: the [compatibility policy][repo-docs-adr-0001-tmux-compatibility-md] and the [field, option, hook and capability reference][repo-docs-reference-catalogue-rakudoc]. ## Watch pane output ### [`ControlConnection.events`][api-connection-events]: receive output through a `Supply` [`Server.open-control-async`][api-server-open-control-async] (or [`Server.open-control`][api-server-open-control]) opens a persistent control connection. Its events are one shared `Supply`, so `react` and `whenever` read them. This program subscribes, sends text with [`PaneRef.send-text`][api-pane-send-text] and checks the screen with [`PaneRef.capture`][api-pane-capture]. ```raku use v6.d; use LibTmux; use LibTmux::Control; sub MAIN(Str:D :$tmux = 'tmux') { my $server = Server.start(:binary($tmux), :name, :shell-command('exec cat')); LEAVE $server.close if $server.defined; my $snapshot = await $server.snapshot-async; my $pane = $snapshot.panes.single.ref; my $connection = await $server.open-control-async(:session-id($snapshot.sessions.single.id)); LEAVE $connection.close if $connection.defined; my $message = 'hello from Raku'; my $received = ''; react { whenever $connection.events.grep(PaneOutput) -> $event { if $event.pane-id eq $pane.id { $received ~= $event.data.decode('utf8-c8'); die 'Pane output exceeded its bound' if $received.chars > 65536; done if $received.contains($message); } } whenever start { $pane.send-text($message); $pane.send-keys('Enter') } { } whenever Promise.in(2) { die 'Pane output timed out' } } die 'The captured screen did not contain the message' unless $pane.capture.decode('utf8').contains($message); say $message; say 'Screen capture confirmed'; } ``` It prints `hello from Raku` and `Screen capture confirmed`. - `send-text` sends literal text; [`send-keys('Enter')`][api-pane-send-keys] submits it. - Output arrives as bytes, so split or invalid UTF-8 survives. More: the longer [session workflow program][repo-examples-session-workflow-raku] also queries and explains. ## Run commands in a batch ### [`Server.run-batch`][api-server-run-batch]: run commands in order, keep every outcome Build a [`Batch`][api-batch] of [`Operation`][api-operation] values. Each one reports `Complete`, `Failed` or `Skipped`. Here the second fails, the third is skipped, and the program removes the first effect itself. ```raku use v6.d; use LibTmux; sub MAIN(Str:D :$tmux = 'tmux') { my $server = Server.start(:binary($tmux), :name, :shell-command('exec cat')); LEAVE $server.close if $server.defined; my $before = $server.snapshot; my $batch = Batch.new(:operations([ Operation.new(:name, :acknowledgement-only, :command(Invocation.new(:argv(['set-option', '-s', '@before-failure', 'set'])))), Operation.new(:name, :acknowledgement-only, :command(Invocation.new(:argv(['libtmux-example-unknown-command='])))), Operation.new(:name, :acknowledgement-only, :command(Invocation.new(:argv(['set-option', '-s', '@after-failure', 'set'])))), ])); my $report = $server.run-batch($batch); die 'Batch attribution was wrong' unless $report.operations.map(*.outcome).List eqv (Complete, Failed, Skipped); my $options = $server.options; die 'The successful first effect disappeared' unless $options.get('@before-failure') eq 'set'; die 'A skipped operation ran' if $options.entries(:name<@after-failure>).elems; say .name ~ ': ' ~ .outcome ~ ' (scope: ' ~ .completion-scope ~ ')' for $report.operations; $options.unset('@before-failure'); die 'Explicit recovery failed' if $options.entries(:name<@before-failure>).elems; say 'Recovery: removed the first effect explicitly'; my $pid = $before.incarnation.pid; my $directory = $server.endpoint.socket-path.IO.parent; $server.close; die 'Owned daemon or socket directory survived cleanup' if "/proc/$pid".IO.e || $directory.e; say 'Owned daemon and socket cleaned up'; } ``` It prints: ```text set-option: Complete (scope: command) invalid-command: Failed (scope: command) skipped-option: Skipped (scope: command) Recovery: removed the first effect explicitly Owned daemon and socket cleaned up ``` A failed batch does not roll back earlier commands. More: the [examples guide][repo-examples-readme-md]. ## Close what you open ### [`Server.close`][api-server-close]: stop a server you started - [`Server.start`][api-server-start] owns a private server; `close` stops it. - [`Server.new`][api-server-new] borrows a server; `close` leaves it running. - Control connections and attachments have their own lifetimes. Close them too. - A reference refuses a replacement server that reuses its ids. ## What it leaves out - **Live objects.** A snapshot is what tmux said when you asked. It does not change when tmux does. - **Rollback.** A failed batch does not undo commands that already ran. - **Callbacks in tmux.** Raku predicates always run locally. ## Support and status - **Experimental.** The API may change between `0.x` releases. The [changelog][repo-changelog-md] marks each break. - **tmux 3.3a or newer.** A release the library does not list yet is refused. - **Linux.** Other platforms are unverified. ## Documentation Headings above link to the native declarations and their RakuDoc comments. - [Native API guide][repo-lib-libtmux-rakumod]: the object graph, queries, capabilities, async execution, control events and recovery. - [Examples][repo-examples-readme-md]: complete Raku programs with checked results. - [Contributing][repo-github-contributing-md]: compiler setup and validation. - [API documentation authoring][repo-docs-documentation-rakudoc] and [writing conventions][repo-github-writing-md]. - [MIT license][repo-license] and [artwork provenance][repo-docs-assets-readme-md]. # libtmux Raku examples
Complete programs that start a private tmux server, do one job and close it. Run them from the repository root after the [toolchain setup](../.github/CONTRIBUTING.md#toolchain), with tmux on `PATH`: ```console $ zef install . ``` | Task | Program | Raku facilities | | --- | --- | --- | | Create and find panes | [Quickstart](quickstart.raku) | Objects, `LEAVE`, a native predicate | | Resize and remove panes | [Resize panes](resize-panes.raku) | `resize`, `kill`, fresh snapshots | | Select wide panes | [Pane queries](query-panes.raku) | Typed selections, query hashes, `grep`, `map`, `sort` | | Choose where a query runs | [Query plan](explain-query.raku) | `explain-panes`, `:pushdown` | | Add a status pane | [Floating panes](floating-panes.raku) | Capability checks and a tiled fallback | | Watch pane output | [Watch output](watch-output.raku) | `Promise`, `Supply`, `react`, `whenever` | | Combine the workflow | [Session workflow](session-workflow.raku) | Events, captured graphs and query plans | | Recover after a command fails | [Batch recovery](batch-recovery.raku) | Typed outcomes and explicit recovery | ## Create and find panes [`quickstart.raku`](quickstart.raku) splits one pane, titles both and finds `editor` in a fresh snapshot. The earlier snapshot still has one pane. ```console $ raku -I. examples/quickstart.raku ``` It prints `editor: 2 panes`. ## Resize and remove panes [`resize-panes.raku`](resize-panes.raku) splits a pane, resizes the window and the first pane, then kills the second pane. A fresh snapshot reads each result. ```console $ raku -I. examples/resize-panes.raku ``` It prints `window: 100x20`, `editor: 30 columns` and `panes: 1`. ## Select wide panes [`query-panes.raku`](query-panes.raku) creates `editor`, `tests` and `logs`. `.where` selects wide panes, `.filter` finds `editor`, `.single` checks the count, and `.grep`, `.map` and `.sort` list the rest. ```console $ raku -I. examples/query-panes.raku ``` It prints `Wide pane: editor` and `Other panes: logs, tests`. - Bind a typed selection with `:=`; `=` copies it into a plain array. - Repeated traversal reads the captured members and does not refresh tmux. ## Choose where a query runs [`explain-query.raku`](explain-query.raku) explains two pane queries, runs one, and shows `:pushdown` refusing the query that keeps a title test local. ```console $ raku -I. examples/explain-query.raku ``` It prints whether each query is fully pushed to tmux, the filter tmux gets, the match, and the refusal. ## Add a status pane [`floating-panes.raku`](floating-panes.raku) creates an empty `status` pane: floating when the daemon reports `pane-floating`, tiled otherwise. ```console $ raku -I. examples/floating-panes.raku ``` It prints `Status pane: floating` or `Status pane: tiled`, then `status`. ## Watch pane output [`watch-output.raku`](watch-output.raku) subscribes to pane-output events, sends text to `cat` and collects the echoed bytes with `react` and `whenever`. Then it checks the captured screen. ```console $ raku -I. examples/watch-output.raku ``` It prints `hello from Raku` and `Screen capture confirmed`. - A deadline bounds the wait. - Several subscribers can share one connection. - Sending text and pressing Enter are separate calls. ## Run the complete session workflow [`session-workflow.raku`](session-workflow.raku) creates panes, sends input, watches control-mode output and captures the screen. It filters a snapshot, then compares an exact source query with the captured pane. ```console $ raku -I. examples/session-workflow.raku ``` The output includes `Session: 2 panes`, `editor: hello from Raku` and `Owned clients, daemon and socket cleaned up`. ## Recover after a command fails [`batch-recovery.raku`](batch-recovery.raku) sets an option, sends an invalid command and checks that the next command was skipped. It then removes the first effect. ```console $ raku -I. examples/batch-recovery.raku ``` It prints the `Complete`, `Failed` and `Skipped` outcomes, then `Recovery: removed the first effect explicitly` and `Owned daemon and socket cleaned up`. A failed batch does not undo commands that already succeeded. ## Select a tmux executable Every program except the quickstart takes `--tmux=PATH`. The quickstart runs `tmux` from `PATH`. The [example check](../scripts/check-examples/check-examples.raku) runs every program against `LIBTMUX_TEST_TMUX`, compares its output and rejects leftover sockets. See [Contributing](../.github/CONTRIBUTING.md#checks).

# tmux compatibility

Status: accepted.

## Decision

Support Linux and the declared stable tmux releases from 3.3a through 3.8.
Use the daemon's version and observed capabilities when selecting commands,
fields, codecs and layouts. A newer client executable does not upgrade the
daemon. Unknown and vendor releases require an explicit support decision.

Keep release profiles in [LibTmux::Catalogue](../../lib/LibTmux/Catalogue.rakumod).
Each profile names its upstream commit. The oldest and newest profiles define
the required live CI jobs; intermediate releases retain pure compatibility
fixtures. Feature boundaries and known defects belong in the field catalogue.

## Rationale

Runtime checks and CI must agree on supported releases. Typed release records
provide one source for both without a separate configuration format. CI verifies
the fetched tag against the pinned commit; it does not need a second inventory
of individual source-file hashes.

Adding a supported release requires reviewing its feature and defect policies,
updating its profile, and passing the relevant fixtures and endpoint tests.
